newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey freezes accounts,securities of Islamic firm.
newsitem.headline: Turkey freezes accounts,securities of Islamic firm.

text.p: A Turkish court on Tuesday froze accounts and securities worth 14.9 trillion lira belonging to the huge Islamist company Kombassan Holding over allegations that it raised capital without consent, court officials said.
The officials said Kombassan had failed to seek the necessary permission for raising capital from Turkey's Capital Markets Board (SPK).
The SPK filed a case over the allegations last week.
"After the application from the SPK we have frozen bank accounts and securities worth 14.9 trillion lira belonging to Kombassan Holding," a official at the Ankara Commercial Court told Reuters.
The diverse Kombassan Holding is involved in printing, paper and machinery production and construction.
The SPK said at the weekend it started legal proceedings against Kombassan, saying "the company attempted to raise its capital without being registered on the board's books."
Kombassan wants to raise its capital to 100 trillion lira from 39.5 trillion -- currently the highest capital held by any Turkish company.

Kombassan, run from Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's stronghold of Konya, caught the public eye when it bought a state tyre company with a higher-than-expected sum in a government sell-off shortly after Erbakan took office last June.
Its activities were highlighted last month when a company courier arriving at Ankara airport was caught, allegedly importing 1.7 million marks ($979,000) illegally from Germany.
